column2:
a man who pursues many romantic or sexual relationships, without following conventional moral rules.
Es un libertino conocido: casi nadie cree que pueda amar con sinceridad.
a female cousin.

a treasured hope or ideal; not merely a visual illusion.
—Hasta un hombre como don Juan necesita una ilusión —nos dice—.

a letter.
Cuando recibe una carta, imagina un camino oscuro.

moral goodness or virtue, as understood by the characters and their society.
Es religiosa y cree mucho en la virtud.

a lamp, here also the image of an enduring hope.
Para él, Estrella debe seguir esperándolo, como la mujer de su imaginación que sostiene una lámpara y nunca se marcha.

a poet; a person who writes poems.
Fausto es un poeta famoso.

one line of a poem.
No escribe ni un verso.

inspiration; the feeling or idea that helps someone create art.
La inspiración

an empty plot of land in a town or city.
Cerca hay un solar vacío, un terreno sin edificios.

a large group of people together.
Delante del solar ve una multitud.

a terrible event that brings suffering or death.
Las personas hablan de una tragedia.

critics or reviewers who judge books, art and poems.
También la crítica lo celebra.
to take something for your own use; here, to treat another person's experience as your own.
a shoemaker; someone who makes or repairs shoes.

a small room where someone is kept in prison.
El zapatero está en una celda.

a priest; a religious man who can hear confessions.
Un grupo de personas escucha al padre Téllez, un sacerdote.

honour or reputation, especially the way other people judge a family; a historically important word here.
El hombre cree que así protege la honra de su familia.
shame or embarrassment, sometimes caused by other people's judgement.

to watch someone closely, often to control what they do.
Cuando ella es mayor, el padre empieza a vigilarla.

a serious unlawful act, such as murder.
—Es un crimen terrible.

to feel sorry about something wrong you have done.
A veces el zapatero parece arrepentirse.
trust; believing that someone will act honestly.
jealousy, especially fear that a partner loves another person.

outward appearances; what other people see and believe.
Felicia tiene que respetar las apariencias.

a short written message.
Entonces veo una cosa pequeña y blanca entre sus manos: es una nota.

a necklace, worn around the neck.
En una mesa veo un collar de perlas.

pearls; small, usually white, valuable objects used in jewellery.
Las perlas son grandes y muy blancas.

a theft; taking something that belongs to another person.
Hablan de un robo.

a report to the police or authorities about a possible crime.
Pronto llega una noticia nueva: un juez recibe una denuncia sin nombre.
revenge; doing harm to someone in response to a perceived wrong.

a regular gathering of friends to talk, read or spend time together.
Esta reunión es una tertulia.
an old-fashioned, often unkind word for an older unmarried woman; it reflects the narrator's social world.

a wig; artificial hair worn on the head.
Lleva vestidos de colores, flores y una peluca rubia.

to read so that other people can hear.
Empiezo a leer en voz alta.
to say goodbye to someone before leaving.

a hug; putting your arms around another person.
Le doy un abrazo muy rápido.
embarrassment or shame.
sympathy for someone else's suffering.
a memory; something from the past that stays in your mind.

a gold box; here, a small precious box that hides a secret.
En su mesa siempre hay una caja de oro muy pequeña.
something a person does not want others to know.
the strong wish to know or discover something.
to pretend; to behave as if something were true when it is not.
a small solid medicine-like tablet; in this story its supposed healing power is uncertain.

a traditional healer, not necessarily a qualified doctor.
Las compro hace tiempo a un curandero de mi pueblo.

to become ill.
Si empiezo a enfermar, tengo que tomar una.
the painful feeling that you have done something wrong.
a person who studies or analyses substances.

the heart; here both a real, beating object in a fantastic story and a symbol of feeling.
El corazón perdido

to beat, as a heart does.
Todavía puede latir.

to wrap something in paper, cloth or another material.
Saco un pañuelo blanco, lo uso para envolver el corazón y lo guardo con mucho cuidado debajo de mi abrigo.

magical glasses; they let the narrator see inside people's chests.
Entonces compro unas gafas mágicas.

the chest, the front of the body above the stomach.
Se pone una mano en el pecho y se va sin escucharme.
to give something back to its owner.

to accept or agree to receive something.
Ninguna quiere aceptar el que llevo conmigo.

jealousy, especially in a personal relationship.
También conoce el miedo, la compasión, el amor y los celos.

to die.
La niña acaba de morir.

a serious problem affecting a blood vessel; in this tale, the doctors’ explanation for the girl’s death.
La examinan y dicen que sufre un aneurisma, un problema grave de un vaso sanguíneo.

a resemblance; when two people or things look alike.
Un parecido

beauty.
¿De dónde viene la belleza?
a sister-in-law; in this story, a man's brother's wife.
a farmhouse and rural estate, especially in southern Spain.
the person responsible for looking after a place or managing work there.
a metal grille across a window or opening.
a story people repeat without knowing whether it is true.
an imagined hope or ideal, sometimes very different from reality.
a relationship between two people who plan to marry; in this historical story it lasts many years.
university studies leading to a qualification; not a race here.
a lawyer, a person who works with the law.

to postpone something to a later date.
La boda vuelve a aplazarse.
a suspicion; an idea that may not be proved.
a strong wish; here it also refers to a woman's need for closeness and love.
a Catholic priest who listens privately to a person's confession.
faithfulness to a partner, including keeping promises of love.

small binoculars used to see the stage or people in a theatre from far away.
Yo llevo unos gemelos de teatro, unos pequeños aparatos para ver mejor desde lejos.
a military unit; the narrator is an army officer.

a man who works at sea; here the young man is a naval officer.
Un día llega a Marineda un marinero joven y elegante, un oficial de la Marina.
suspicions, beliefs that have not been proved.

a woman employed to help in a household; a historical occupation.
Una criada guarda la ropa de las dos jóvenes en la playa.

waves moving across the sea.
Hay mucha espuma y es difícil verlas entre las olas.

to drown; to be unable to breathe in water.
Me grita que empieza a ahogarse.

an injury or wound.
Está muerta y tiene una herida en la frente.
an account or story told by a particular person; not necessarily a proven version of events.

a place where people stay temporarily in tents or other simple accommodation.
Montaron un campamento cerca de un barrio nuevo.

fortune-telling, an attempt to predict the future.
La joven le ofreció leerle la mano mediante una adivinación.

to mistreat someone, physically or otherwise.
Ayudó a la muchacha a ponerse en pie y dijo al hombre que podía denunciarlo por maltratar a su esposa.

someone who sees an event or can give information about it.
No había un testigo que hubiera visto el crimen ni una prueba que identificara al culpable.
to suspect; to consider something possible without proof.

the body of a person; here, the body of a woman found dead.
Unos pastores habían encontrado, en una sierra lejana, el cuerpo de una mujer muy joven.

an inquiry into the facts of an event, especially a crime.
Se abrió una investigación.
a belief that an event or sign can bring good or bad luck without reliable evidence.

a coincidence; two events that happen together without a demonstrated causal link.
Una coincidencia que no puedo olvidar.
a hunting trip.

a curse; words intended to bring someone bad luck.
Entonces pronuncia una maldición:
a shotgun used for hunting.

to fire a gun.
Sin saber que allí estaba su hermano, decidió disparar.

a roe deer, a small wild deer.
Creyó ver un corzo y levantó la escopeta.

guilt or responsibility for doing something wrong.
Santiago murió, y Leoncio quedó destruido por la culpa.
a masked ball, where guests often wear costumes.

a mask covering the eyes and part of the face.
»Llevaba un antifaz negro y un manto que le cubría parte del cuerpo.

to force somebody to leave a place or group.
Al final bajó al salón para expulsar a Natalia.

what other people generally say or believe about someone.
Tenía mala reputación.
a widow / widower; a person whose spouse has died.

to feel pity or sympathy for somebody.
»Él empezó a compadecerla.
to marry without telling others.
tuberculosis, an infectious illness historically also called *tisis*.

a female singer; here, a professional theatre performer.
Laura es una cantante de teatro.

a type of musical theatre performance, sometimes called an operetta.
Cuando canta en una ópera cómica, el público la escucha con alegría.
jealousy; fear that someone you love is interested in another person.
a dressing room for performers at a theatre.

a threat; words or actions that suggest someone may cause harm.
Comprende que sus palabras son una amenaza seria.

an architect, someone who designs buildings.
Busca a un arquitecto y le pide un edificio extraordinario.

a large and important church.
El rey quiere construir una catedral muy hermosa.
a contract, a work agreement.

to leave or go away.
Pierde dinero por marcharse antes de tiempo.

a promise, a commitment about what someone will do.
Le hizo una promesa.
a person who hopes to marry or have a romantic relationship with someone.
a wedding ceremony.

a farewell; here, one delivered in a letter.
Era una despedida.

a country property with a house and surrounding land.
Sus padres la llevaron a una finca familiar en el campo, lejos de las conversaciones y las miradas de la ciudad.
a betrayal, breaking someone's trust.

a religious house; staying there does not necessarily mean becoming a nun.
Una semana después, en Marineda se supo que Martina se había instalado en un convento de Compostela.
shame; the painful feeling of being exposed, humiliated or unable to accept something about oneself.

a traditional grocery shop selling food and imported goods.
En una ciudad pequeña hay una tienda de ultramarinos muy famosa.

a shop assistant or employee.
También trabaja allí Germán, un dependiente joven.
a storeroom where a shop keeps its goods.

a fire that spreads and causes serious damage.
Durante la noche prepara un incendio y cierra las salidas que su mujer podría utilizar para escapar.
smoke; the dark or grey gases from a fire.

a key used to open and close a door.
Cuando Germán está dentro, el dueño cierra la puerta con una llave.

blame or responsibility for something bad.
Nadie le atribuye la culpa.
to suspect; to think something may be true without proof.
to lose almost all one's money or business.

an angel, a heavenly being; here the central character is an actual angel.
Un ángel comete una falta en el cielo.
exile, being forced to live away from one's home.
a daisy, a small flower with white petals.

a newspaper.
En el suelo encuentra también un periódico.
iron bars fitted across a window.

jasmine, a plant known for its scented flowers.
Sobre todo, recuerda el olor del jazmín.

to escape or run away, often secretly.
La muchacha decide escaparse.
a slap across the face.
a reputation; what other people believe about someone's behaviour.

a military unit stationed in a town.
Allí había una guarnición del ejército español.

a lieutenant, an officer of junior rank.
Él era muy amigo de Ramiro Quesada, un teniente joven, valiente y alegre.
a captain, a military officer of higher rank than a lieutenant.

a statement given formally to a court or authority.
Pero aquellas palabras eran la confesión de Ramiro, no una declaración de ella.

a military court that judges offences involving service members.
Un consejo de guerra reunió las pruebas y lo interrogó.

a court's formal decision and punishment.
El tribunal dictó una sentencia de muerte.

to execute a person by shooting; a historical form of capital punishment.
Al amanecer del día siguiente iban a fusilar al teniente.
a woman whose spouse has died.

a confession; an admission of something personal, often troubling.
Por eso quiero hacerte una confesión.
remorse; a painful feeling about something one believes one has done wrong.
a marquis; a hereditary noble title used in the historical setting of the story.
evidence that can support or contradict a claim.

a formal fight between two people to defend their honour; a historical practice.
Si viene a buscar un duelo, no voy a esconderme.

to watch or keep someone under observation.
Pero siempre he procurado vigilar a Leonor.

a ghost; here also an imagined love affair that seems real to the person experiencing it.
—Es como si un fantasma de amor hubiera tomado mi nombre y mi aspecto —dijo.
a suspicion, something one thinks may be true without knowing it for certain.

a painted portrait; in this story, an image that seems to reveal someone's character but does not.
Era el retrato de una mujer.
great-grandmother.
an estate or piece of land belonging to a family.
jealousy, especially fear or anger about another person's affection.

a private room used for prayer.
Los dos llevaron el cuerpo, las sábanas y el arma al escondite que había debajo del oratorio.

an axe.
Magdalena sostenía la vela mientras el campesino lo mataba con el hacha.

to confess; to admit something that has been concealed.
Quería confesar todo y que lo llevaran ante la justicia.

prison.
Pasó muchos meses en la cárcel.
a portrait or photograph; three portraits introduce the story's family relationships.

an orphan; a child whose mother and father have died.
La huérfana se llamaba Mercedes.
godfather; also a familiar form of address for a trusted older protector in this story.
unfaithfulness within a romantic relationship or marriage.

pregnant.
Mercedes estaba embarazada.

smallpox, a serious contagious disease.
Contrajo las viruelas, una enfermedad grave y contagiosa.

the passing of an illness from one person to another.
El contagio terminó con su vida.

blame, guilt or responsibility for a wrong action.
Hipólito reconocía parte de la culpa, pero continuaba justificando sus decisiones.
a nobleman holding the title of viscount.
an adult legally responsible for a child and sometimes for the child's property.
a niece, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

to give something up deliberately.
En lugar de eso, decidí renunciar a ella.
a duty or something one believes must be done.
a refusal, especially of an invitation or a proposal.
regret about something one has done.
remorse, painful regret linked to one's actions.

a spa or health resort; here, a place where seriously ill people sought treatment.
En un balneario elegante se alojaban dos jóvenes muy enfermos.
a room immediately next to another.

Christian communion, a religious rite in which believers receive the consecrated bread.
Un día, las personas que los cuidaban les propusieron recibir la comunión.
a soul; the spiritual part of a person in the belief system of the story.

heaven.
Ella era una luz azul, ligera y clara, que se dirigía hacia el cielo.

purgatory; in Catholic tradition, a state of purification before heaven.
Su destino era el purgatorio.
a flame.

the tall pole on a ship that supports sails or equipment.
Su pequeña luz aparece algunas noches sobre el mástil de un barco, muy lejos de la tierra.
St Elmo's fire, a luminous electrical phenomenon sometimes seen around ships' masts.

a community where nuns live a religious life.
Cuando recuperó las fuerzas entró en un convento, lejos de su pueblo.

a nun; a woman who belongs to a religious community.
La iglesia estaba en silencio y, detrás de una doble reja, vi a una monja muy anciana.
a metal grille separating two spaces; here, part of the convent.
an inn where travellers can stay.

a poet; someone who writes poetry.
En el mismo pueblo había nacido Juan de Camargo, un poeta que pronto sería famoso.

lines of a poem.
Aquella noche Camargo escribió unos versos y los arrojó a la ventana de la joven, envueltos alrededor de una piedra.

a bet; an agreement involving a challenge or a possible reward.
Entonces hizo una apuesta cruel: demostrar que podía vencer la resistencia de Irene.

to humiliate; to make someone feel ashamed or publicly degraded.
Camargo había preparado la situación para humillar a Irene delante de todos.
acts of religious repentance, sometimes involving severe self-denial.
